conditions.sentence: The durable task record contained a section for items awaiting the user, which made relaying an item feel equivalent to preparing it.
No user-facing item carried an acceptance criterion.
The rule that would have prevented this was enforced by attention rather than by machinery.

diagnosis.sentence: The assistant asked the user to carry out a manual verification task more than once in a single session without preparing the artifact the task required.
No locations within it were specified.
In the same session the assistant produced detailed, self-contained briefs for its automated sub-agents.
The asymmetry is the defect: the human executor received the least prepared instruction.

disclosureHeading: This is exactly what your Rich would report. In this version it is written to this machine and nowhere else; nothing in RichOS can carry it any further.

failureClass.label: The assistant handed the user a task it had not prepared.
The assistant left the user to notice a failure that machinery should have caught.
The assistant left the user to ask whether a class of failure would recur.
The assistant asked the user a question whose answer was already determined.
The assistant left the user to sequence work it should have sequenced itself.

options: 1: Bad | 2: OK, but could be better | 3: Good | 0: Dismiss
question: How is RichOS doing this session?
reportOffer: Will you let your Rich tell the RichOS developers — fully anonymized and generically — what annoyed you and why it happened?
